newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq buying from Syria under U.N. oil deal - papers.
newsitem.headline: Iraq buying from Syria under U.N. oil deal - papers.

text.p: Iraq has signed its first contracts with Syrian firms under its oil-for-food deal with the United Nations, newspapers said on Sunday.

"The Trade Ministry signed yesterday with Syrian companies several contracts to supply Iraq with foodstuffs under the memorandum of understanding (oil deal)," the government newspaper al-Jumhouriya said.
The paper said Syrian firms would supply large quantaties of wheat, pulses, soap and detergents. It gave no details.
"Signing such contracts is the beginning of trade activity between the two sisterly countries which would cover other aspects in the future," the paper said.

The United Nations on Wednesday renewed the 180-day deal under which Iraq can export $2 billion worth of oil to pay for humanitarian needs and reparations to the victims of Baghdad's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
Purchases from Syria would arrived via the Iraqi-Syrian highway that had been closed since the early 1980s when the states severed diplomatic ties over the Iran-Iraq war.

Jumhouriya said the head of Iraq's Chambers of Commerce Federation Zuhair Abdul-ghafur would lead a delegation to Damascus on June 15 to complete talks started in Baghdad last month. A Syrian business delegation was in Iraq in May.
Syrian ties with Baghdad deteriorated in 1980 when Damascus backed Iran in the 1980-88 Iraq-Iran war and worsened when Syria joined the U.S.-led force that drove Iraqi troops from Kuwait.

The official al-Qadissiya newspaper said Lebanese businessmen were in Baghdad trying to sell food and medicine. The paper quoted delegation head Nabil al-Ladhiqi as saying that reopening the road between Iraq and Syria would facilitate the supply of Lebanese goods to Iraq.
